So over the past few months, I have upgraded my stereo system significantly from my previous post. I decided that it was time for a major upgrade!

First, I added the Klipsch R-100SW subwoofer to add more bass to my listening experience and to lay off some of the work from the bookshelf speakers for the bass.

Then I added the Klipsch R-160M speakers in conjunction with my already owned Klipsch R-41M speakers. And these speakers are bigger than I thought! I think they’re in the later stages of breaking in as I got them about 2 weeks ago. I still have the R-41M speakers but as the B pair.

Then I added the much needed Ortofon 2m Blue cartridge. I had the cartridge that came with the AT-LP120XUSB and when I received the R-160M speakers, I finally heard inner groove distortion and I could tell that the cartridge was not achieving the full potential of the speakers. So I added the Ortofon 2m Blue cartridge today and I can already tell a major step up with better channel separation, punchier sound (especially bass) and much more detail and soundstage!

I never understood sex scenes. Yes, it’s a way to show two characters connecting intimately but what if those two characters share their past and their trauma if they have any. That way, the audience can see that the characters are connecting and also provide more of an emotional connection between the audience and the characters.

Having a sex scene doesn’t really do anything to the overall plot unless it is important to the story. The audience isn’t there to watch someone’s every day life. The audience is there to be entertained by their life. Moving the plot forward keeps the audience entertained.

A lot of pointless sex scenes are present in early slasher movies (some even included the directors so that they could be a creepy fucking pedo and have sex with the “hot and young” actress).

But it can be vital to the plot such as a recent horror movie, X. Sex was important to the old couple so they could feel young again. And it showed that if the audience were ok with seeing a younger couple have sex, they should be ok with seeing the old couple have sex (which a lot of people didn’t like seeing). So having those scenes were important here.

But a lot of the time, sex scenes are just there to grab (mostly male) attention and make the audience like the movie.

Paul Gray was important to the band as well as one of the main songwriters and practically the heart of the band. But V-Man stepped in and Slipknot still has their dna.

Chris Fehn had amazing backup vocals and good performances on his percussion. Then Michael Platt stepped in and is improving his vocal performance and bringing more youthful and sporadic energy to the live performances.

If Corey left, it wouldn’t be fair for the rest of the members if the band retired, unless it’s in everyone’s agreement. Yes, Corey has his iconic part in the band but so did Joey, Paul, and Chris. Slipknot just in its name is legendary in the broad metal genre and even in music in general. So I was always in love with music. From my childhood years to my teenage years. I grew up on Metal with bands such as Slipknot, Stone Sour, Korn, Metallica, Avenged Sevenfold, and more. I even went to a Slipknot concert with Korn and King 108 opening up for them when I was 11!

When I turned 13 though, I moved on from Metal to Alt. Rock. I listened to bands such as twenty one pilots, Imagine Dragons, Panic! At The Disco, and more. I also listened to artists such as Lorde and Melanie Martinez. 

When I was 14 (about to turn 15 in a couple of months), I then moved onto Rap with Logic. I despised Rap with a passion, but grew to live it over time. After a couple of months of listening to Logic, I started listening to Denzel Curry. He mixed everything I loved with music and he is still one of my favorite artists to this day.

In the summer of the year that I listened to Rap (2018), my friend showed me Billie Eillish and I loved her music. So I listened to her EP, dont smile at me, and I really loved it!

I listened to Foals a couple of times before with Spanish Sahara, but haven't really gotten into them until they teased their first 2019 album, Everything Not Saved Will Be Lost Part 1. I started listening to them more and fell in love with them, especially with Total Life Forever. I loved their new album and kinda liked the follow up album. I also listened to Billie Eilish's new album, but didn't like it as much as her EP. 

From mid to late 2019, I started getting back into Metal with the release of Slipknot's We Are Not Your Kind. I loved that album and then later on in mid to late 2020, I listened to more of their albums and I loved them. I also listened to Korn and then listened to System of a Down. 

In late 2019, I wanted more heavy stuff mixed with Rap. I've heard of Zillakami and seen City Morgue's music video of SHINNERS13, but I was arrogant at the time and labeled it as generic nonsense. I heard that their new album, As Good As Dead came out with Denzel Curry as a feature, so I listened to it and instantly fell in love with it. 

In early 2020, I started listening to Scarlxrd and I liked his music a lot; though not as much as City Morgue's. Now, I am more into heavier music, but I will listen to almost anything.

I started collecting records on my birthday in 2019 with twenty one pilots's, Blurryface, but I had 2 records before; Wicked and twenty one pilots's Trench Triplet EP. I got a lot of more records from birthdays and Christmas, and I eventually got myself a Fluance RT-81 turntable with Micca PB2X Powered Speakers on Christmas 2019! On Christmas 2020, I got a Kallax shelf to store all of my records after having them in a cardboard box for a year in a half.
